A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PerturbODE, with matching core methods and experiments. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and additions.

before.justification: V4 reports original simulation benchmarks, TF Atlas network recovery, held-out perturbation predictions, ablations, and module analyses.

after.justification: V6 retains original empirical results and adds longitudinal knockout experiments, additional network validations, component ablations, and computational measurements.

M1.justification: The core ODE architecture, intervention mechanisms, and original losses remain unchanged. V6 Appendix A.7 introduces a time-series adaptation that aggregates Wasserstein losses across observed time points, extending the training objective for longitudinal data.

E1.justification: V6 adds actual evaluation on longitudinal hiPSC Perturb-seq data with 23 CRISPR knockouts, four time points, and 103 analyzed genes (Section 6.2 and Appendix A.7). SERGIO and TF Atlas remain; BEELINE (BoolODE) is the retained cyclic simulation benchmark under revised naming.

E2.justification: RENGE is newly evaluated against PerturbODE on longitudinal data in Figure 8. Explicit RANDOM reference baselines also appear in AUPRC comparisons. GENIE3, GEARS, scGPT, and the original causal discovery baselines were already evaluated in v4.

E3.justification: The main ChIP-Atlas AUPRC evaluation changes from 223 shared genes to 79 development-related genes; a 41-gene GO-selected evaluation is added, while the full 223-gene evaluation remains in Appendix A.13. New protocols include top-50 upregulated-DEG F1 evaluation, pseudobulk comparisons, five-perturbation time-series batches, and CPU-only runtime comparisons.

E4.justification: V6 adds direct ablations removing L1 regularization, replacing Wasserstein loss with pseudobulk MSE, and extracting networks through a three-layer MLP saliency map (Tables 13–15). It also adds solver and learning-rate sensitivity checks and module-count AUPRC analysis. Earlier threshold, perturbation-count, and bootstrap stability analyses are retained.

E5.justification: V6 explicitly attributes five-run comparisons to different seeds and data splits, including TF Atlas comparisons whose earlier captions lacked this information. This expands disclosure without establishing increased run counts. The 105-bootstrap and 133-split stability analyses remain unchanged.

E6.justification: V6 adds longitudinal, development-specific network, DEG, ablation, and computational results. For example, Table 13 reports AUPRC of 0.017 without L1 versus 0.022 with L1 on all 223 shared genes. Original Table 2 prediction scores and matched simulation statistics remain unchanged; the new 79-gene scores do not establish a same-setting improvement over v4.

T1.justification: V4 leaves a rigorous ODE identifiability proof to future work. V6 adds Theorem A.1 and a proof using stationary-density equations, spanning score differences, normalized factors, and rank assumptions, claiming identification up to permutation and sign symmetries. This substantially expands the formal theory.

C1.justification: The five principal introduction contributions remain. Prediction is more cautiously framed: v4 concludes that unseen cellular responses can be predicted accurately, whereas v6 emphasizes demonstrating feasibility and describes perturbation prediction as an extension in the abstract.

C2.justification: V6 links its ChIP-Atlas advantage specifically to developmental genes and explicitly acknowledges comparable GENIE3 performance on the full 223-gene network, qualifying v4's general superiority interpretation. The longitudinal discussion also identifies substantially higher variability and the need to improve stability.

D1.justification: V6 adds PerturbODE's Adam optimizer and 10^-4 learning rate, reference-gene selection details, longitudinal batching instructions, and CPU profiling information. Appendix A.26 supplies a planned code repository address where v4 only promised release. Most existing hyperparameters and hardware disclosures remain; neither PDF establishes that the promised code is available.

R1.justification: V6 substantially expands developmental-genetics citations and biological justification for the selected validation genes in Appendix A.11. It adds RENGE, GO, and implementation references and discusses Bicycle's Gaussian-distribution limitation. Publication updates and the renamed attribution of the existing SDE-identifiability reference are not new works.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion are rewritten; network inference and perturbation prediction become separate Results sections; and the appendices are extensively reorganized. Broader impacts move into the main back matter, acknowledgments are added, and the NeurIPS checklist is removed.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column layout, with extensive resizing and rearrangement of displays. V4 Figures 9 and 10 become combined Figure 11, and the full ChIP-Atlas comparison moves from main Figure 5 to appendix Figure 15. New longitudinal plots and sensitivity, DEG, runtime, and ablation tables expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: V6 strengthens empirical scrutiny through component ablations, DEG evaluation, longitudinal testing, and computational measurements. However, it replaces v4's explicitly unresolved identifiability proof with a guarantee whose stated assumptions do not justify a key step: Theorem A.1 permits constant nonzero second derivatives, for which Equation 25's asserted nonzero rank-one difference vanishes. The empirical gains coexist with this unresolved theoretical guarantee, preventing a reliable overall quality judgment.
